title: The request carries the data
summary: A form submission is an HTTP request: read $_GET and $_POST, validate, then escape.

blocks.html:
When a visitor submits a form, the browser sends an ordinary HTTP request whose fields are name=value pairs. The form's method decides where those pairs travel: GET appends them to the URL as a query string, POST puts them in the request body.

Use POST for anything private. A GET URL is kept in browser history, in server access logs, and in every proxy in between — a PIN in a query string is a PIN you have published.

blocks.title: where the fields go
blocks.ascii:
GET  /atm_withdrawal.php?pin=1234&action=verify
       ^ one URL. Saved in history, logs, Referer.

  POST /atm_withdrawal.php
       action=verify&pin=1234
       ^ the body. Not in the URL, not in the log line.

  Same PHP file handles both. Only the method differs.

blocks.title: which method arrived
blocks.code:
<?php

if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'POST') {
    echo 'This is a form submission.', "\n";
}

echo 'Method: ', $_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'], "\n";
blocks.output:
This is a form submission.
Method: POST

blocks.html:
PHP fills two arrays before your first line runs. $_GET holds the query string, $_POST holds the parsed body. Both are ordinary arrays of strings — a submitted 1234 arrives as the string "1234", so cast before you compare numbers.

Neither array contains a key the browser did not send. Reading a key that is not there is the most common warning in PHP.

blocks.title: the same script, nothing submitted
blocks.code:
<?php

$pin = $_POST['pin'] ?? '(nothing sent)';
$amount = $_POST['amount'] ?? '0';

echo 'pin: ', $pin, "\n";
echo 'amount: ', $amount, "\n";
echo 'fields in the body: ', count($_POST), "\n";
blocks.output:
pin: (nothing sent)
amount: 0
fields in the body: 0

blocks.html: Drop the ?? and $_POST['pin'] on a request without a pin gives Warning: Undefined array key "pin" and the value null. The page still renders, which is exactly why this warning survives so long in production. ?? or isset() is the two-character fix, and it forces you to decide what a missing field means.

The ATM page in this project is one handler with two steps, both POST to the same file. The action field says which: verify checks the PIN and reveals the amount box, withdraw spends the money. Every field is cast to its type and then checked against a rule — the browser's min, max, and required attributes are advice, and advice can be skipped with a single curl command.

blocks.title: step 1: verify the PIN
blocks.code:
<?php

$action = $_POST['action'] ?? '';
$pin = (int)($_POST['pin'] ?? 0);
$message = '';
$isPinValid = false;

if ($action === 'verify') {
    if ($pin !== 1234) {
        $message = 'Access Denied. Incorrect PIN.';
    } else {
        $isPinValid = true;
        $message = 'PIN accepted. Enter an amount.';
    }
}

echo 'PIN valid: ', ($isPinValid ? 'yes' : 'no'), "\n";
echo $message, "\n";
blocks.output:
PIN valid: yes
PIN accepted. Enter an amount.

blocks.title: step 2: withdraw the amount
blocks.code:
<?php

$balance = 5000.00;
$amount = (float)($_POST['amount'] ?? 0);
$message = '';
$withdrawn = null;

if (($_POST['action'] ?? '') === 'withdraw') {
    if ($amount < 100) {
        $message = 'Please enter a valid withdrawal amount minimum of 100.';
    } elseif ($amount > $balance) {
        $message = 'Insufficient Funds!';
    } else {
        $balance = $balance - $amount;
        $withdrawn = $amount;
        $message = 'Withdrawal Successful!';
    }
}

echo $message, "\n";

if ($withdrawn !== null) {
    echo 'Amount Withdrawn: ', number_format($withdrawn, 2), "\n";
    echo 'Remaining Balance: ', number_format($balance, 2), "\n";
}
blocks.output:
Withdrawal Successful!
Amount Withdrawn: 1,500.00
Remaining Balance: 3,500.00

blocks.title: echoing user input back
blocks.code:
<?php

$pin = $_POST['pin'] ?? '';

echo '<input type="number" name="pin" value="', htmlspecialchars($pin), '">', "\n";
echo 'raw length: ', strlen($pin), "\n";

blocks.html: Validation and escaping are different jobs. Validate on the way in — cast, range-check, reject. Escape on the way out — htmlspecialchars() turns <, >, &, and quotes into entities so the browser shows the text instead of running it. Escape at the moment you print, not when you store, and pass the same raw value to htmlspecialchars() every time you echo it.

quiz.q: Where are the fields of a GET form submission?
quiz.why: GET appends name=value pairs to the URL. POST puts them in the body, which is why POST is the choice for a PIN.

quiz.q: The handler reads $_POST['pin'] and the request arrived without a pin. What happens?
options: A fatal error stops the page
A warning about an undefined array key, and null is used
The key is created with an empty string
quiz.why: PHP 8 emits Warning: Undefined array key, then evaluates the expression to null. The page keeps rendering, so use ?? to choose a default on purpose.

quiz.q: A visitor submits the name Bob<script> into a field you echo back. What keeps that harmless?
options: htmlspecialchars() at the point you print it
Saving the value to the session first
quiz.why: Escaping on output turns the angle brackets into entities, so the browser renders text. Casting does not remove markup.

exercise.brief: A form posts pin and amount to this script. Print PIN ok when the pin is 1234, otherwise PIN rejected. When the pin is correct and the amount is between 100 and 5000 inclusive, print Dispensed: followed by number_format($amount, 2); otherwise print Amount rejected.
exercise.starter:
<?php

// $_POST is already filled from the submission
$pin = (int)($_POST['pin'] ?? 0);
$amount = (float)($_POST['amount'] ?? 0);

// print the two lines
exercise.hint: Keep the answer in a variable: $valid = $pin === 1234. Then echo ($valid ? 'PIN ok' : 'PIN rejected'), "\n"; and use if ($valid && $amount >= 100 && $amount <= 5000).
exercise.solution:
<?php

$pin = (int)($_POST['pin'] ?? 0);
$amount = (float)($_POST['amount'] ?? 0);

$valid = $pin === 1234;

echo ($valid ? 'PIN ok' : 'PIN rejected'), "\n";

if ($valid && $amount >= 100 && $amount <= 5000) {
    echo 'Dispensed: ', number_format($amount, 2), "\n";
} else {
    echo 'Amount rejected', "\n";
}
